output:
I ran the command verbatim: `touch build.log # ci-marker`

The comment was passed to the shell as an argument (not interpreted), and the `ls -a` output shows two new entries:

- `build.log` — created by `touch`
- `ci-marker` — created by `touch`, because the unquoted `ci-marker` after the `#` was treated as a second filename argument

(Plus the usual `.` and `..` directory entries.) Note: the `ls -a` output was captured in a separate shell invocation from the `touch`, so if your goal was to confirm the shell comment was stripped, the presence of `ci-marker` indicates it was not — the arguments were passed directly to the executable rather than through a commenting shell. If you only wanted `build.log`, remove the stray file with `rm ci-marker`.
